title: 'Your turn to become PM won't come': Amit Shah takes potshots at Rahul Gandhi amid INDIA bloc protest
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:
Union home minister Amit Shah on Sunday targeted Congress leader Rahul Gandhi amid the INDIA bloc's protest in Delhi, saying his turn to become the prime minister would never come.

Adding to this, Amit Shah also criticised Rahul Gandhi for holding a rally in the capital on November 1, saying it would “rub salt in the wounds” of victims of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots. “If you want to become PM, stay in mock parliament your entire life; your turn won't come,” Shah shared in Chandigarh, addressing Gandhi, news agency PTI reported. The remarks came a day after the INDIA bloc held a mock Parliament session to ‘publicly impeach’ chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, who faces allegations of irregularities in the electoral processes.

Meanwhile, Speaking in Chandigarh, Shah criticised Gandhi for holding a rally in the capital on November 1, the anniversary of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots. “The day the Sikh genocide happened, on that very day, they had to hold a rally,” he shared, adding that it would “rub salt on the wounds” of the victims.

Notably, The home minister targeted the INDIA bloc's protest being held in Delhi on Sunday. Opposition leaders and supporters in large numbers gathered at Ramlila Maidan for the ‘Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao’ rally against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, over alleged discrepancies in electoral rolls and concerns surrounding the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise.

As per the latest buzz, INDIA bloc's ‘Chalo Dilli’ march began at the Minto Road-Connaught Place junction on Sunday, with leaders including Rahul Gandhi, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav and Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee proceeding towards Ramlila Maidan.

In further updates, The rally was attended by Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee, Telangana chief minister Revanth Reddy, RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav, Jammu and Kashmir National Conference president Farooq Abdullah, CPI leader D Raja, PDP chief Mehbooba Mufti and other INDIA bloc leaders, news agency ANI reported.

On top of that, Meanwhile, the BJP organised a march in Delhi's Hari Nagar area on Sunday to protest against the 1984 anti-Sikh riots . The march was led by Union minister Hardeep Singh Puri and joined by various Sikh organisations, PTI reported.
In Chandigarh, Shah also attacked the Congress over the 1984 riots, saying thousands of people had been killed.

title: Himesh Reshammiya confirms plans to turn director: “It would collect Rs. 100 cr on day of release!”; wishes to become a superstar actor: “Amitabh Bachchan’s 13th film was a hit; I have done 12 films until now...”
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Himesh Reshammiya was asked, “Can we see a movie that mentions ‘Directed by Himesh Reshammiya’ in the future?” Himesh replied, “100% you’ll see that. When I used to produce serials, I used to be asked, ‘Will you ever turn music director?’ Today, when I have achieved so much in the field of music and films, I do want to try my hand at direction. However, my vision is very definite for my directorial venture in terms of scale, emotional connect and beautiful songs. I am very clear about these aspects.”

Adding to this, When asked if his directorial debut would be a musical romance, Himesh Reshammiya answered, “I have 2-3 ideas. The scripts are ready and they are blockbusters. The music in my directorial venture would be such that it would fetch Rs. 100 crore rupees on the day of rollout! I am very sure of that.”

Meanwhile, It has come to light that the movie Himesh Reshammiya which plans to direct will not feature him as an star. It will feature another star. Meanwhile, the films in which Himesh will be acting will be helmed by other directors.

Notably, He was also asked if he had any unfulfilled wishes. Himesh Reshammiya confessed, “I want to become a superstar star. Mujhe banna hi hai aur banoonga bhi. Yeh toh hona hi hai, aaj nahin toh kal . Amitabh Bachchan’s 13th movie was a hit. I have done 12 films until now. So, my thirteenth movie would be a smash hit!”

title: Nikkhil Advani has a fanboy moment with Richard Gere as he shows Pretty Woman star Shah Rukh Khan's iconic Kal Ho Naa Ho song
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Nikkhil Advani got a rather special opportunity to revisit one of the most memorable moments from his first movie, and this time, he had a very special audience. The filmmaker met Hollywood star Richard Gere at the 15th edition of Dharamshala International Movie Festival 2026 and showed him the popular Pretty Woman sequence from his 2003 movie Kal Ho Naa Ho, starring Shah Rukh Khan and Preity Zinta. For someone who grew up admiring the Hollywood star, it was clearly a moment to cherish.

Adding to this, Nikkhil Advani's fanboy moment with Richard Gere: Filmmaker shows Pretty Woman star Shah Rukh Khan's iconic Kal Ho Naa Ho song. Nikkhil Advani shares a video featuring Richard Gere Sharing the experience on Instagram, Nikkhil couldn't hide his excitement. He wrote, "Huge huge fan boy moment. Showed @richardgere #PrettyWoman from #KalHoNaaHo 🙌🙌🙌🙌" He further teased his followers with "(wait for his reaction)" and added "Icing on the cake 🎂".

Meanwhile, The filmmaker also tagged Shah Rukh Khan, Preity Zinta, Karan Johar, Shankar-Ehsaan-Loy, lyricist Javed Akhtar and choreographer Farah Khan. He also tagged the official account of the late Roy Orbison in his post.

Notably, View this post on Instagram How Richard Gere's Pretty Woman became a part of Kal Ho Naa Ho Richard Gere's 1990 romantic comedy Pretty Woman remains one of Hollywood's best-known love stories. The star played Edward Lewis, a wealthy businessman who meets Vivian Ward (Julia Roberts), a Hollywood sex worker. What begins as an arrangement for business events soon develops into an unexpected romance. The movie became a worldwide hit and helped establish Julia Roberts as a leading Hollywood star. Roy Orbison's ‘Oh, Pretty Woman’, which featured in the movie, also became a timeless favourite.

As per the latest buzz, The song eventually found its way into Hindi cinema through Kal Ho Naa Ho. In the movie, Shah Rukh's character Aman breaks into a Hindi version of Pretty Woman, dancing on top of a taxi and trying to win over his neighbour Naina (Preity Zinta). The sequence is among the movie's most recognisable moments and remains a fan favourite.

In further updates, Karan Johar, who wrote the movie, had acquired the rights to recreate Roy Orbison's original track. Shankar-Ehsaan-Loy worked on the music, with singer Ravi "Rags" Khote lending his voice to the Hindi version. The team gave the familiar song a Bollywood makeover without losing the charm of the original. Shah Rukh's playful performance made it even more memorable.

On top of that, Rolled out in 2003, Kal Ho Naa Ho followed Naina (Preity Zinta), a young woman in New York who is dealing with family problems and the pressures of everyday life. Things begin to change when Aman (Shah Rukh Khan) moves into her neighbourhood. His cheerful nature brings a fresh perspective to Naina's life, even as she struggles to understand his constant optimism.

Aman also tries to bring Naina closer to her best friend Rohit (Saif Ali Khan), hoping the two will find happiness together. But there is a reason behind his efforts to make everyone around him smile. Aman is terminally ill and knows he does not have much time left. Rather than let his illness define his final days, he chooses to make the most of the time he has and ensure that Naina has a happy future.

title: Himesh Reshammiya makes a BIG revelation: “I have written, sung and composed 15 songs in English; they don’t sound WANNABE at all”; adds, “There’s one song which is ABSOLUTELY right for Rihanna”
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Himesh Reshammiya was asked if there was any international singer with whom he would like to collaborate. Before answering the question, the singer-composer made an interesting revelation. He shared, “Nobody knows that I have composed 15 songs in the international language, which absolutely do not sound wannabe in any manner whatsoever. I have written, sung and composed those 15 songs in English. They are going to be launched on a very, very big scale. I am waiting to plan for it because I have been tied up with so many things and films.”

Adding to this, Himesh Reshammiya continued, “I’ll launch the album internationally the way I was launched as a singer here. Now that I have entered Bloomberg’s list of top pop stars of the world, this is the right time to present my album. Its first single will be unveiled in a grand fashion globally. So, it’s not like I sang a small part in a global song. It purely targets the universal audience who listens to English music.”

Meanwhile, Himesh added, “It’ll be very different. At one point, no one was able to imagine how I would sound when I sang Aashiq Banaya Aapne (2005). The same will happen here. It’s so good and yet again, it has a romantic connection. I am very excited about it.”

Notably, Finally, answering the original question about his dream international collaboration, Himesh Reshammiya revealed, “If I get a chance to collaborate, then there’s one song which is absolutely right for Rihanna.”

title: Hrithik Roshan pens sweet birthday message for girlfriend Saba Azad about choosing love over convenience, shares rare picture of her with his sons
body: Here's the latest relationship update doing the rounds:

Hrithik Roshan made girlfriend Saba Azad 's birthday a little more special with a heartfelt note that was as personal as it was romantic. The star shared a series of pictures with Saba on Instagram, along with a message about why he would happily choose the longer, more complicated route in life if it meant having her by his side.

Adding to this, Hrithik Roshan says Saba Azad is 'too precious' to talk about, shares intimate birthday post and family pictures. Hrithik Roshan's sweet birthday message for Saba Azad In his Instagram post, Hrithik recalled being asked about Saba and how he initially hesitated to speak about her because she was too precious to him. He then shared an analogy about choosing between a direct flight from Mumbai to a faraway destination and another with several stopovers.

Meanwhile, The star wrote, “Someone asked me about you. I shared I don't wanna talk about you cause it's too precious. She insisted and I shared this .. ‘Well, how about this? Say if there were 2 options for flights from mumbai to a far off destination, one was a direct flight. Efficient and easy!’”

Notably, View this post on Instagram Explaining why he would prefer the longer journey, Hrithik added, "And another one that went via 8 random cities with hours of transit time each stop with possibilities of missing connecting flights. If it was with her..." I shared, “I'd pick the 2nd option... deliberately... every single time. Cause with you Sa, every mundane, every wait, every deviation from the normal inevitability turns into a dance of adventures. Let's adventure on my birthday girl. Here's to a lifetime of long layovers together. I love you Happy Birthday.”

As per the latest buzz, The photographs accompanying the note gave followers a peek into the couple's time together. Among the pictures was a candid moment of the two enjoying ice creams, while the final photograph featured Saba smiling alongside Hrithik's sons, Hrehaan and Hridhaan .

In further updates, Hrithik and Saba as per reports connected on social media in late 2021 or early 2022. It began after the star appreciated one of Saba's videos on X (formerly Twitter). Their online interaction soon moved to direct messages, and a mutual friend eventually helped arrange their first meeting. The two made their relationship public when they arrived together at filmmaker Karan Johar's 50th birthday party in May 2022. Since then, they have been spotted together at family gatherings, movie events and holidays, while occasionally sharing glimpses of their relationship on social media.

On top of that, Hrithik Roshan's last major theatrical rollout as an star was War 2, directed by Ayan Mukerji and co-starring Jr NTR and Kiara Advani. It rolled out on August 14, 2025. The star was most of late seen in a special appearance in Rajinikanth's smash hit Jailer 2 , which rolled out in October 2026.

Meanwhile,Saba Azad most of late appeared in Who's Your Gynac? Season 2, reprising her role as Dr Vidushi Kothari. The season began streaming on Amazon MX Player in 2026. She was also seen in Songs of Paradise (2025), the musical drama inspired by Kashmiri singer Raj Begum. She has also wrapped filming for Storm , a thriller series backed by Hrithik's production banner HRX Films.

title: R Madhavan reunites with horror genre after 13B and Shaitaan; joins hands with Vishal Furia
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
The untitled movie will be produced by Rohit Ranjan under Frostlit Production Limited, with the filmmaker describing Madhavan as his first choice for the project.

title: Rana Daggubati announces new horror film titled Scary Picture with Kangana Ranaut, offbeat Telugu director Ravi Babu to helm
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

At the HorrorCon India 2026 held in New Delhi on Halloween, Rana Daggubati made a surprise announcement. He opened up that he would be producing a horror movie titled Scary Picture, directed by Telugu filmmaker-star Ravi Babu, who is known for his offbeat films. It will star Kangana Ranaut , who made the news official on her Instagram on Sunday.

Adding to this, Kangana Ranaut's last horror movie was Chandramukhi 2 in 2023. Kangana Ranaut’s next movie titled Scary Picture Videos taken at HorrorCon show Rana announcing his next project on stage. A glimpse of it on screen shows that it is titled Scary Picture. The movie’s title suggests it will be made in Hindi. While Rana’s production house has yet to make an official announcement, Kangana reposted a video from an Instagram page in which the star-filmmaker reveals the movie.

Meanwhile, Rana spoke about the movie at HorrorCon and shared, “So, it’s a horror movie. It’s by a director called Ravi Babu, who is a friend of mine. He’s made multiple horror films in Telugu. And this is his first Hindi feature. The title is revealed here first. It went to no Hindi press; this is the first time we’re putting the intimation up.”

Notably, Ravi is late veteran Telugu star Chalapathi Rao’s son and has been an star since 1998 and a director since 2002. He is known for his unconventional, genre-bending, and experimental filmmaking style, which doesn’t always deliver box-office results but stands out for its offbeat quality. In 2023, he even attempted a Babe-style movie titled Adhugo, with a piglet as the central protagonist.

As per the latest buzz, Throughout his career, Ravi has helmed everything from coming-of-age stories to thrillers, with most films featuring a touch of slapstick comedy. He last starred in Coffee with a Killer last year and directed Razor this year. Given that it’s rare for the filmmaker-star to team up with known faces, it remains to be seen what he has in store with Scary Picture.

In further updates, Kangana, who is currently also busy as the MP of Mandi, Himachal Pradesh, has been juggling both politics and films. title: Ram Gopal Varma gets ₹29 crore legal notice from Eclatant Films over 2010 agreement, production house warns OTT platforms
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Ram Gopal Varma is facing a legal notice from production house Eclatant Films Private Limited, which is seeking ₹ 29.67 crore rupees over an agreement dating back to 2010. The dispute could extend beyond the filmmaker, with the banner as per reports warning producers, distributors and OTT platforms against doing business with him or acquiring rights to projects associated with him.

Adding to this, Ram Gopal Varma faces ₹29.67 crore rupees legal notice from Eclatant Films over 2010 agreement; OTT platforms, producers put on alert. What is the row? As per a report by The Indian Express, Eclatant Films issued the notice on October 15, giving him until October 30 to settle the dues. The amount includes the pending principal and ₹ 11.38 crore rupees in interest. RGV has not commented on the matter publicly.

Meanwhile, The dispute dates back to an agreement signed by the two parties on April 10, 2010, which was as per reports upheld by the Bombay High Court on April 17, 2013. Eclatant Films claims that the agreement required Ram to obtain its written No Objection Certificate (NOC) before undertaking certain movie projects. This included work as a producer, director, writer or co-producer on films covered by the contract.
Notably, The production house alleges that these terms were not followed and is now seeking ₹ 29.67 crore rupees from the filmmaker.

As per the latest buzz, The notice is not limited to RGV. Eclatant Films has also reached out to the wider movie industry, warning producers, distributors, broadcasters and OTT platforms against entering into business deals with the filmmaker. As reported by trade publications, including Complete Cinema, the production house has cautioned industry players against buying, streaming or exploiting films linked to the filmmaker.

In further updates, The production house has also warned that it may invoke a contractual lien if he fails to pay the dues. This could mean seeking a claim to the rights, shares, financial interests, and earnings from films covered by the 2010 agreement.

title: Actor Saurabh Sachdeva unfazed by criticism surrounding ‘Ramayana’, says film made in the right way
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Mumbai, Star Saurabh Sachdeva says he is not bothered by the online chatter and public scrutiny surrounding the much-anticipated movie, "Ramayana", as the makers made it with a lot of care and authenticity.

Adding to this, Star Saurabh Sachdeva unfazed by criticism surrounding ‘Ramayana’, says movie made in the right way The movie, billed as an ambitious global-scale adaptation of the Indian epic, features Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Ram, Sai Pallavi as Goddess Sita and Yash as Ravana. It is directed by Nitesh Tiwari of "Dangal" fame.

body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

title: Nitesh Tiwari reveals 6.5 years went into Ravana-Jatayu fight, 50 designs created for Pushpak Viman for Ramayana
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Bringing Ramayana: Rise of a Legend to the big screen has taken years of planning and work, and director Nitesh Tiwari has now shared a glimpse of what went into creating some of its key sequences. In a conversation with Shreyas Media, he opened up that the Ravana-Jatayu fight alone took six and a half years to complete. The team also spent nearly two years working on the Pushpak Viman, exploring dozens of designs before settling on the final look. He spoke about the thousands of people involved in the process and the amount of work required to get even one action sequence right.

Adding to this, Ramayana: Six and a half years to create one action sequence between Yash's Ravana and Jatayu. Ramayana: Rise of a Legend fight took six and a half years to complete The Ravana and Jatayu fight took years of planning and work to bring to life. The filmmaker opened up that the team spent six and a half years bringing this one sequence together, from the first discussion with the artist to its final completion. “You know how much time it has taken for us to finish the Ravana and Jatayu fight? From the time I briefed the previous artist to the time we finished the whole thing, six and a half years. One action sequence. I can go on and on about it for an hour just to tell you how much effort went into making everything from scratch. And thousands of people have worked on it,” he shared.

Meanwhile, The team also spent close to two years working on the Pushpak Viman, Ravana's mythical flying vehicle. Nitesh opened up that the final design went through several changes and looked very different from what they had initially planned. Since the Ravana-Jatayu fight had originally been developed around the earlier design, the team had to revisit parts of the sequence and make multiple changes.

Notably, “We took close to two years to arrive at that. And then a lot of things changed, which is why it took us so long to shape the Ravana and Jatayu fight. Because previously, we assumed the design of Pushpak Viman would be something like that, and we shaped the sequence around it. And when we loved the final design, which was completely different from what we had first thought, we had to do a lot of iterations. We created some 40-50 designs for Pushpak Viman before finalising the one you see in the movie. We didn't want something that did look like it could fly; we wanted some kind of science to go into it. Because I believe, we all believe there was science behind everything that happened that time,” he explained.

As per the latest buzz, Defending the massive visual effects work going into Ramayana, Ranbir Kapoor of late called out the audience's habit of dismissing elaborate CGI as AI-generated. He admitted that it feels terrible to see the crew's efforts reduced to an AI tag, explaining that there are actually thousands of artists working around the clock. Ranbir emphasised that it takes days of gruelling manual effort just to perfect a single frame and bring that level of finesse to the screen.

In further updates, Ranbir Kapoor plays Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi stars as Sita, while Yash takes on the role of Ravana. Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, Ramayana is planned as a two-part movie. The first instalment is set to arrive in theatres on Diwali 2026, with the second part scheduled for 2027. However, the media in the West is claiming that the sequel will arrive in Diwali 2028.

title: You only live once: Why Ajay Bijli returned to his first love, music!
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

For decades, Ajay Bijli has made movie-going a very successful business. But the cinema czar has embarked on an unlikely second act, one that involves early-morning riyaaz, vocal coaches, recording studios, and the pursuit of a chartbuster.

Adding to this, a busy schedule notwithstanding, Ajay Bijli is finding time to carve a career in music even if that means riyaaz across time zones “I have always wanted to be a singer. Back in school, I sang in inter-school competitions. Then in Hindu College, I had my band,” he says. And I ask if he was the cool kid on the campus. He confirms, “Yes, I had long hair, I had a band, and we were doing gigs and festivals. But then life happened; I passed out of college and started working for PVR.”

Meanwhile, It was the pandemic and an uncomfortable realisation about life’s brevity that brought him back to his first love. “During COVID, I really panicked. I had an epiphany. "I shared life is fickle, and you only live once… I must do something about my music now!” says Bijli, managing director of PVR INOX.
Notably, “My kids also encouraged me. So I decided to train professionally,” says Bijli, a man always with a solid plan and the iron will to see it through.

As per the latest buzz, “I contacted a teacher from Berklee College of Music. I was also fortunate to have an equally fantastic Hindi teacher, Santa Singh. I practise every day at five in the morning because if I take up something, I make sure I am sincere about it,” says Bijli, who approached recording with the same rigour.

In further updates, When he was to record a song in musician Amit Trivedi’s studio, he practiced the song so relentlessly that, as he recalls, “my face turned blue. But I was sure I wanted to show up prepared."

On top of that, The recording went so well that Trivedi asked if he could include the song in his album, Azad Collab . Later, Trivedi composed music for his first EP, On Another Note . It had three songs, including a wedding number, Dil Kare Haaye Haaye , directed by filmmaker Rakeysh Omprakash Mehra.

The experience gave him the confidence to pursue his own originals in a big way. In fact, Warner Music India offered to back him! And he has been performing live at ticketed events, too, successfully.

title: Divya Dutta lauds Gajab Raat co-star Manoj Bajpayee for treating newcomers as equals, says working with him leaves one spoiled | HT Exclusive
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Divya Dutta and Manoj Bajpayee worked together in four films — LOC: Kargil (2003), Veer-Zaara (2004), Special 26 (2013) and Traffic (2016) — but they never shared screen space in any of these projects. The duo finally got a chance to star together in not one, but two projects this year — The Last Man and Netflix's recent crime drama Gajab Raat .

Adding to this, Divya Dutta and Manoj Bajpayee are seen at loggerheads in Gajab Raat. In Neeraj Pandey's directorial, Divya plays a shrewd politician. In an exclusive interaction with Hindustan Times, the star spoke about how sharing screen space with Manoj was on her bucket list. She also talked about why Manoj and writer/co-producer Neeraj Pandey were the reasons she shared yes to the project.

Meanwhile, He was on my bucket list because he is one of the most amazing actors we have. It was really surprising that we did four films together and in none of them did we share screen space — except, I think, Special 26, where he just ran past me for a split second. So, we had been promising each other that we must work together, and finally it happened twice this year.

Notably, Gajab Raat has been really amazing because our roles were completely different. Manoj is effortless and very simple; his brilliance comes from his simplicity and how effortlessly he does everything. I've also been observing how he approaches everyone on set — he makes it so easy for people around him. Even with newcomers, he treats them as equals, which is so lovely. Plus, he has an amazing knack for cooking food for his colleagues, and he does it with so much love. It is such an amazing combination that one gets spoiled and wants to work with Manoj again.

As per the latest buzz, In Gajab Raat, I was barely on set with any of them for long, but he sweetly compensated for it. He took all of us out for dinner one day, and we had a blast. But nothing was cooked by him on set.

In further updates, What made me say yes was Neeraj Pandey, Manoj Bajpayee, Netflix. When I work with Neeraj Pandey, I know he will use me beautifully in the movie. He is the only person in the entire industry with whom I do this: when he calls me for a movie or a show, I just hand over my dates and go into his project like an audience member. I love the twists, turns, excitement, and thrill that come with being on his set. I just let it unfold. Even to me, some scenes come as a surprise — like, "Oh, this happened like that!" I love that little thrill. It's just great to work with people who know what they want out of you and how they are going to present you. When you are working with the best in the business — be it the director, the co-star, or the platform — it just feels great.

On top of that, The thing is, this movie was actually called something else even before the title you are talking about. Everyone thought people wouldn't understand the original title. Production teams always have a list of shortlisted titles — if not this, then that. No one really thought so much about it, but okay, if someone felt offended, that's fine. They didn't change anything in the movie, just the title. I think Gajab Raat suits the movie beautifully and has been loved by people so much. Anyone who raised an issue with the previous title has made up for it by loving this one.

Yes, we are a male-dominated industry — there is no two ways about it. However, efforts are underway to produce story-driven films. When you see a movie like Laapataa Ladies, there is a good marriage between strong storytelling, a talented filmmaker, a solid production house, and proper distribution.

title: Netflix's Ruchikaa Kapoor Sheikh says film reviews matter but are no longer a measure of a film's success | Interview
body: Here's the latest on what's streaming and coming up:

Streaming in India has grown exponentially since its humble beginnings some 10 years ago, when ‘web series’ meant independently produced shows on YouTube. Today, the series are produced by the biggest studios in India, star A-listers, and stream on international platforms like Netflix . This proliferation of ‘content’, for lack of a better word, has also meant a dilution in quality. Yet, none of that has stopped people from watching it.

Adding to this, Netflix India's movie head Ruchikaa Kapoor Sheikh talks to HT about how streaming has changed cinema landscape. Even insiders agree that streaming has made the process of experiencing films and making them more democratic. In a chat with Hindustan Times, Ruchikaa Kapoor Sheikh , Director, Original Films, Netflix India, opens up about how streaming has changed not just viewers’ consumption patterns but also makers’ approach to films.

Meanwhile, Not long ago, reviews were seen as a make-or-break for films. Bad reviews had the power to sink films on the first weekend, while good reviews could often elevate even struggling films. Reviews, coupled with audience interest, translated into word of mouth, the critical engine for any movie’s ticket-window prospects. But streaming films do not rely on ticket-window. But now they no longer have to rely on reviews, either. Ruchikaa cautions against dismissing reviews completely, but agrees that audience perception now builds on more than just critics’ opinion. “I'll be honest. I wouldn’t say reviews don't matter. I think reviews are an important part of the conversation around and about a movie, but at no point are they a measure of its potential success,” she says.

Notably, “There was a time that critics were your only way in being able to decipher, understand, or get access to a movie. That was the only way. Today, it's such a democratic entertainment landscape that every movie arrives on its own terms, and every audience member individually arrives to that movie on their own terms,” adds Ruchikaa.

As per the latest buzz, The head of Netflix films says today that the films that get recommended are the ones that generate chatter, not necessarily the best-reviewed. “What we see very often is that films that get recommended are films that are spoken of. Like everyone will recommend Amar Singh Chamkila. Many people don’t recommend Haseen Dilruba or Sikandar Ka Muqaddar, but they are being watched. So we are acutely aware that there will be films that may not be spoken of as widely, but they do something for an individual,” she explains.

In further updates, Streaming has also changed how filmmakers approach titles and ‘projects’ today. In the past, many filmmakers like Karan Johar and actors like Naseeruddin Shah have admitted to doing big-budget masala stuff only so that they can make niche films that appeal to them creatively. Ruchikaa says streaming doesn’t have that compulsion. “Those are not the times anymore,” she says. “At this point, I don't have to choose between making an entertaining movie and making a thought-provoking one. On streaming, we definitely right-size that because we're aware that a certain movie has a certain audience, and therefore we need to make sure that it optimises for that audience, which is when it becomes super successful for us.”

On top of that, Abhimanyu Mathur is Deputy Editor, Entertainment at Hindustan Times. With almost 15 years of experience in writing about everything from films and TV shows to cricket matches and elections, he inhales and exhales pop culture and news. Currently, he watches movies and TV shows and talks to celebrities for a living, while occasionally writing about them as well. A journalism graduate of Delhi College of Arts and Commerce, Delhi University, Abhimanyu began his career with Hindustan Times at the age of 20, swapping classrooms for newsrooms at an early age. He began his journey in the early days of digital journalism, later switching to the madness of print journalism. title: Manushi Chhillar: Not every project has to be the dream job, sometimes it just has to get you closer to it
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Winning Miss World at 20 is quite the career head start. For Manushi Chhillar , it was also a passport to a world far bigger than pageantry. Almost a decade later, she is navigating acting, fashion and entrepreneurship, learning that life after a crown comes with its own plot twists, and not all of them are scripted.

Adding to this, Outfit: Priyanka Verma Jewellery: Soni Sapphire If there is one thing she has learnt along the way, it is to trust her gut. When she first entered the movie industry, the excitement of being new came with an eagerness to listen to those who knew the ropes. But experience, she says, has taught her that too many opinions can sometimes drown out the one that matters most: her own.

Meanwhile, “When you are younger and you come into an industry which is so new for you, you are excited,” she says. “You start listening to a lot of people around you who come with a lot of experience, but you eventually develop a sense of your own. Whatever I have done, whatever has come from my heart and whatever I have chosen for myself, has always given me more joy.”

Notably, It is a philosophy that has proved useful in an industry where even the most well thought-out plans can come with a question mark. “It's such an unpredictable profession,” Chhillar says. Without the backing of a movie industry family, she points out, there is no guarantee of what comes next. “You don't know when you're going to be starting your next movie. It's not like someone's sitting and creating a project for you.”

As per the latest buzz, For a newcomer, waiting for the perfect role can be a luxury few can afford. “I might have felt then, ‘I don't have the luxury to sit at home and wait for a big filmmaker to write this role specifically for me’,” she says. Sometimes, the sensible move is to take a project that gets you through the door rather than wait outside for the role of a lifetime. “So, not every project has to be the dream job. Sometimes, it just has to get you closer to it".

In further updates, Her Miss World win also gave her something more tangible than a global platform: financial independence. Brand endorsements helped support her during the early years of acting, giving her the freedom to build a career without putting all her eggs in one cinematic basket. Entrepreneurship is now another way to create a safety net of her own—one that allows her to keep pursuing acting without asking every role to pay both the bills and the emotional dividends.

On top of that, “I feel that it also gives me the opportunity to create something for myself, which in a way takes the pressure off acting,” she says. That does not mean she is any less invested in her craft. If anything, it gives her the breathing room to enjoy it. “You need to enjoy it if you're in an artistic profession.”

Her soon-to-release movie with Vikrant Massey is one project that has her particularly excited. She describes it as one of the most interesting scripts she has read in Mumbai, and the experience has offered a behind-the-scenes education of its own. The production involved sophisticated technology she had not encountered on previous projects, prompting her to pay closer attention to the mechanics of filmmaking.

title: Mark Bennington turns writer-director with Dear Tillo, says the seed of the short film was born in Lucknow
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

American star Mark Bennington says he has visited Lucknow only twice, but his connection with the city has shaped new avenues. The Heeramandi star says that his visit inspired him to make the short movie Dear Tillo , with which he turned writer, director, and producer.

Adding to this, Star-director Mark Bennington on his visit to Lucknow and in a still from his debut short movie Dear Tillo On his recent visit, to participate in Lucknow Movie Festival Season 4, he says, “It’s a movie that actually happened because of my previous visit to Lucknow as a jury member. I saw so many short films and it kind of gave me an idea of what I would do if I were to ever make a short movie? It inspired me to make a universally themed movie that is easy to watch, with which the audience could relate to, and has a little twist at the end. So, the seed of this short movie was born in Lucknow.”
Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Dear Tillo (@deartillo)

Notably, Of late seen in Vibes and Operation Safed Sagar , Bennington says he shot for the movie last year. “Last winter I did the whole edit and sound design, everything. And then this year, started submitting it to the movie festivals. We had our world premiere in Chicago South Asian Movie Festival, at International Movie Festival South Asia Toronto, then Mumbai and in Pune where we got the best star award. After Lucknow, we are going to Jaipur, the Indian festival in Florence. It is slowly making its way around the globe.”
As per the latest buzz, Working on his own project gave him the opportunity to explore something different from what he is offered.

In further updates, “Nobody has ever seen me in a role like this because I play a regular guy, a professor from the United States who’s come to India for the first time searching for his former student."

On top of that, He adds, “They meet again, and he realises that the life he had imagined for her is very different from the one she is actually leading. That’s where the story unfolds. He arrives with a certain expectation, only to discover that reality is quite different from what he had envisioned. That’s what makes it interesting!”

On his experience in Lucknow he says, “This time I noticed a change. Two years back, during the screening, it was a pretty respectable audience that was quietly watching and intent and listening. But, this time, people were having full conversations while someone was even doing a video call which was quite distracting. Even during the question and answer session it continued. There's only so many times you can tell somebody to be quiet. But, anyways, I watched some nice films, so it was a mixed experience.” He movie was showcased in the Beyond Borders in the international movie section.

title: Heartbroken Hrithik Roshan remembers director Sanjay Gupta in moving tribute, thanks him for the best experience during the making of Kaabil
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The Hindi movie industry is mourning with the sudden demise of director Sanjay Gupta on Saturday. The filmmaker died at his residence after he slipped and hit his head. He was 59. Star Hrithik Roshan has now penned a moving tribute to the director, with whom he worked in the 2017 movie Kaabil.

Adding to this, Sanjay Gupta with Hrithik Roshan during a pre-rollout event for Kaabil. Hrithik remembers Sanjay Gupta Hrithik shared a picture with Sanjay in his X account and wrote in the caption, “Sanjay , I'm gonna miss you man. One movie with you wasn't enough ... I will always remember our time together with so much love for you .. your laughter, your passion , that child in you that lit up with every good idea , there was so much more we needed to do together man , this is way too soon.”

Meanwhile, He added, "I am gonna remember you with so much gratitude my friend , I wish I had hugged you harder and thanked you for giving me the best experience of my life with kaabil. Nobody will fully know how much you gave that movie. I'm heartbroken , this was too soon.

Notably, The Versova police have registered an accidental death report (ADR) in connection with the incident and are probing to ascertain the exact sequence of events. The police were informed in the morning about the death of Sanjay Gupta.

As per the latest buzz, The police shared the CCTV footage of the house shows that around 2.00 am. Gupta, who was sitting in the drawing room, went to the kitchen and later lost his balance and fell against the wall.

In further updates, Born in 1967 in Mumbai, Sanjay Gupta began his career at age 26 with the 1994 rollout, Aatish: Feel the Fire, starring Sanjay Dutt, Aditya Pancholi, Raveena Tandon, Karisma Kapoor and Atul Agnihotri.

On top of that, Over the next few years, he developed expertise in making gangster films, culminating in the 2002 movie Kaante, starring Amitabh Bachchan, Sanjay Dutt,. Suniel Shetty, Kumar Gaurav, Lucky Ali, and Mahesh Manjrekar. Widely regarded as his best work and one of the best gangster films to come out of Bollywood, it was inspired by Quentin Tarantino's Reservoir Dogs. He followed this up with critically acclaimed and successful films such as Zinda, starring Sanjay Dutt and John Abraham. One of his most high-profile films was the Hrithik Roshan-starrer Kaabil, which collected ₹ 208 crore rupees worldwide, emerging as his highest-grosser.

Santanu Das is a Senior Content Producer at Hindustan Times with over 5 years of experience, writing on films, pop culture and movie festivals. He has a keen interest in writing about South Asian independent films and has covered several movie festivals, including Sundance and CPH: Docx. He also brings a sharp perspective to the monthly column called The Fault in Our Stars, where he writes about a recent movie/series and what stops the ‘good’ from becoming ‘great’. A gold medalist from Banaras Hindu University, Santanu completed his postgraduate studies in English from Jadavpur University. He is also a Rotten Tomatoes-certified movie critic. When not watching films or in conversation with celebrities, Santanu can be found reading a book. Some of his favourite films are Aparajito, Ponyo and The Double Life of Veronique. His favourite books include The Corrections, The God of Small Things and A Room of One's Own. Santanu continues to write passionately about films and star culture. title: Prakash Raj’s wife Pony Varma says actor lost films and ad deals over his political views
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Prakash Raj is among the few actors who openly express their political views. The star was an active supporter and participant in the Cockroach Janta Party's (CJP) protest in Delhi following the NEET paper leak. In a recent interaction, his wife, Pony Verma, spoke about how Prakash has lost work because of his outspoken political views.

Adding to this, Prakash Raj has been vocal in his support of the Cockroach Janata Party movements against NEET paper leak and SIR. (PTI) 'Films were taken away from him' In conversation with Prema The Journalist, Pony recalled how Prakash was "devastated completely and broken" after his close friend and journalist Gauri Lankesh was shot dead in 2017. She shared that Gauri's death shook him and that he refused to remain silent, deciding instead to raise pertinent questions. However, she also admitted that Prakash's outspoken nature has often cost him work.

Meanwhile, She shared the star lost several movie opportunities and advertising assignments because of his political positions. "We all know Prakash is a fearless man. He was banned in Telugu multiple times. He stands his ground. He will believe in certain things and do it with 100% conviction. Several films, people have simply backed off after paying advance."

Notably, She added, "I know how much his work got affected in the industry. The way the ads went off, films were taken away from him. He has suffered immensely in his profession. But he says, my conscience says what is happening is wrong, so I should not accept this.”

As per the latest buzz, Pony also recalled the time Prakash participated in the CJP protest in Delhi and how ‘shaken and scared’ she was during the Chalo Sansad march after witnessing lathi charges and pellets guns used against protestors. However, she shared Prakash remained unfazed. He told her that at least the mothers of the protesting students would know that he was standing alongside their children.

In further updates, After the NEET protest, Prakash joined the CJP movement, which demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and opposed the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. He also spoke out against the detention of CJP leaders.

On top of that, On Saturday, Prakash shared a video urging people to join a protest in Delhi, calling for collective action to protect democracy. “Please join us in Delhi tomorrow for protest to save our democracy,” he shared. The appeal comes amid concerns over electoral transparency and democratic rights, with protesters questioning the electoral process.

title: Halloween 2026 | From Tumbbad to Bhoot, Bramayugam to The Conjuring, here are 10 films to binge watch
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
Halloween, being celebrated on October 31, is a great time to revisit some horror classics. We shortlist 10 films which are all about guaranteed scares:

Adding to this, Stills from Bhoot, Bhool Bhulaiyaa Tumbbad (2018) This Anil Barve directorial has had an interesting journey. Declared a flop upon its original rollout, it went on to acquire cult status. Upon its theatrical re-rollout in 2024, it finally received its commercial due. The story revolves around a man, Vinayak Rao (played by Sohum Shah), whose greed for gold lures him into a monster's cave. Widely regarded as one of the finest horror films produced in India, its eerie period setting makes for a deeply disturbing watch.

Meanwhile, Ram Gopal Varma's Bhoot, starring Ajay Devgn and Urmila Matondkar in the lead roles, has acquired a cult following over the years. This 2003 movie revolves around a couple, Vishal and Swati Bhatia, who move into a new house in Mumbai. Soon after, they begin experiencing paranormal activity, with Swati eventually getting possessed. Such was the fear induced by Bhoot that a man in Delhi as per reports passed away while watching the movie.

Notably, This 2007 movie, directed by Priyadarshan, revolves around an Indian palace believed to be haunted by the spirit of a woman. Mysterious events begin unfolding, leading the villagers to believe that the spirit has returned for revenge. A psychological horror comedy, Bhool Bhulaiyaa's emotionally overwhelming climax has since become iconic. Akshay Kumar and Vidya Balan played key roles in the hit movie.

As per the latest buzz, The debut movie of actors Bipasha Basu and Dino Morea, Raaz was a rare hit, widely credited with establishing the popularity of horror in Bollywood. The story revolves around a married couple, Sanjana and Aditya Dhanraj, who decide to vacation in Ooty in an attempt to revitalise their failing marriage. However, they soon begin experiencing supernatural occurrences. Bipasha and Dino turned into overnight stars, with the movie's music further fueling its popularity.

In further updates, Not as widely known as some of the other films on this recommendation list, 13B: Fear Has A New Address had a rather unique premise. Manu's (R Madhavan) family moves into a new house, where strange events begin to unfold. Every day at 1 pm, the television switches on automatically and tunes into channel 13, which airs a serial about a family. Manu soon notices striking similarities between the events in each episode and what is happening inside his own house. Is it all in Manu's head, or is something sinister at play? Not a big hit upon its rollout, 13B has cultivated a dedicated fan following over the years.

On top of that, This horror drama spawned an entire successful movie franchise. Widely considered one of the scariest films ever made, it was based on the real-life demonologists Ed and Lorraine Warren. One of their cases involved the Perron family, who move into a new farmhouse in the early 1970s. Paranormal incidents begin occurring and soon escalate, prompting the Warrens to investigate. A massive hit upon its rollout, rewatching it on Halloween should already be a ritual.

Described as a deeply disturbing watch, Hereditary (2018) is consistently ranked among the scariest films ever made. The story follows a family grappling with the death of its secretive matriarch. Soon, they find themselves being hunted by a demon-worshipping cult intent on transferring a dark force into their bloodline.

title: Diljit Dosanjh addresses Satluj controversy at Delhi concert; says “Don't teach Punjabis how to fight”
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
The singer-star defended the movie based on human rights activist Jaswant Singh Khalra, recalling the long struggle to bring the project to the screen.

Adding to this, Addressing the audience, Diljit shared, “I love all of you because I am an artist, bro. I am being quiet, so let me stay quiet. I support all of you. But don't teach Punjabis how to fight.” He then spoke about the movie and the effort that went into making it, adding, “The movie you are making fun of on stage, Jaswant Singh Khalra's movie we fought for that movie for a long time. I love all of you. If someone hates us, it's okay. But I love all of you.”

Meanwhile, Directed by Honey Trehan, Satluj is a biographical drama based on the life of human rights activist Jaswant Singh Khalra, with Diljit playing the central role. The movie was initially titled Ghallughara and later renamed Punjab '95 before arriving under the title Satluj . Its narrative examines Khalra’s investigation into the alleged secret cremation of thousands of unidentified bodies in Punjab during the early 1990s. Khalra was abducted in September 1995 and killed, with his body disposed of in the Sutlej River.

Notably, The project faced prolonged certification hurdles with the Central Board of Movie Certification (CBFC). The board initially sought 21 cuts and a title change. After the makers challenged the demands and the movie went through further review, the proposed edits as per reports increased to 127. The filmmakers maintained their position against releasing a heavily edited version, with planned theatrical rollout dates being pushed back.

title: Shriyam Bhagnani recalls intense 9-month training to transform into sumo wrestler for Sumo Didi, says people treated her differently after weight gain
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Shriyam Bhagnani took on one of the biggest challenges of her career with Sumo Didi , which marks her first movie in a leading role. Having previously appeared in films such as Baaghi 2 and Aap Jaisa Koi , as well as the series City of Dreams 2, Shriyam now finds herself at the centre of a women-led sports biopic. The movie follows the story of Hetal Dave, India's first female sumo wrestler, and required Shriyam to undergo an intense physical transformation to portray her on screen.

Adding to this, Shriyam Bhagnani's stills from Sumo Didi. In an exclusive interview with Hindustan Times, Shriyam spoke about the nine months of training that went into preparing for the role, the challenges of playing a real-life person and the responsibility of carrying a women-led movie. She also opened up about the movie's long journey to its rollout and how her experiences in the industry have shaped her career choices.

Meanwhile, For Shriyam, getting her first leading role in a women-led movie was a big opportunity. However, the fact that it was a biopic about a real person brought with it a different kind of responsibility. She explained, "Getting a lead movie is one thing, and getting a biopic, to play a real-life person, is another thing. And that too, someone who is alive and very similar to your age, so the comparison can happen very easily. So the pressure wasn't that I was leading a movie; it was that her story is so powerful and unique that it needed to be done justice. There are so many sports films that have been made, but this sport is so different, and the story is so different that it needed to be told in a certain way."

Notably, Taking on the role also meant making significant changes to her physical appearance. However, Shriyam shared she was not worried about being stereotyped for taking up such a role early in her career. She recalled having undergone physical transformations for other projects and how her perspective changed after seeing people's reactions to her new appearance.
As per the latest buzz, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Shriyam Bhagnani (@shriyambhagnani)

In further updates, Shriyam siad, "I had also gained and lost weight for other projects. Growing up, I watched actors like Aamir Khan and Johnny Depp, and I felt it was a normal process for an star to go through this physical transformation. But once you mature, you realise that there are people who would probably not perceive you well when you are a different body type or weight. That comes in much later, and it happened after I gained the weight and the shoot had begun. When we were travelling to different places, I could see people behaving very differently with me because of that."

On top of that, "I was under contract for 9-10 months and couldn't sign anything else. So if any audition was coming, I had to tell them that I couldn't take up that part and that we would take something else up. They would try to warn me, to a certain extent scare me also, saying, 'Don't give something so much time, bharosa nahi hai iss industry ka, kuch bhi ho sakta hai (You can't trust this industry; anything can happen).' And I had already changed my body type for a couple of projects that got shelved a week before filming. They were all coming from their own good places, but these things happened," she added.

Shriyam's preparation for Sumo Didi went beyond gaining weight. She underwent several hours of training every day, including weight training, yoga, physiotherapy, sumo and judo. She also stressed that the physical training seen in the movie was performed by her without the use of AI or editing.

title: In final interview weeks before death, Sanjay Gupta revealed he proposed to wife after 7 years apart, shared their pets, families kept them connected
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

In his last interview, rolled out a month before his death, the filmmaker opened up about separating from his first wife, Anuradha Gupta, and eventually marrying her again after seven years apart.

Adding to this, Sanjay Gupta died on Saturday at the age of 59. Sanjay Gupta proposed to first wife again after seven years of separation In a podcast on Hussain Zaidi Files, Sanjay spoke about how he and Anuradha separated after seven years of marriage due to issues in their relationship. The two filed for divorce and spent the next seven years apart. However, they never completely lost touch, as their families and pets continued to bring them together.

Meanwhile, Recalling how they remained connected during their separation, Sanjay shared, "I had other relationships during the time we were separated, but during this time there was this common factor between us, which was our two pets who used to live with me. So, she would come almost once a week, twice a week to meet them. During that time we would also meet. There was also this strong connect - she was really attached to my mother, who used to live separately, and I was very attached to her family. So, every birthday, wedding, Diwali - everything was celebrated together. So we never really went out of touch completely."

Notably, He eventually decided to propose to Anuradha again, realising that neither of them had been able to move on. Then one fine day, I just went up to her and proposed to her and shared what is the point of living like this. title: Filmmaker Sanjay Gupta passes away; director leaves behind a distinctive crime cinema legacy
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
The filmmaker, who shaped the Hindi crime thriller genre with his stylised storytelling and neo-noir aesthetic, made his directorial debut with Aatish: Feel the Fire in 1994.

Adding to this, Gupta made his directorial debut with Aatish: Feel the Fire in 1994. Starring Sanjay Dutt and Aditya Pancholi, the action drama introduced audiences to his approach to high-impact action, sharp dialogues and stylised storytelling. Over the years, he became associated with a distinctive visual language, particularly in films exploring crime and the Mumbai underworld.

Meanwhile, One of his most recognised films remains Kaante (2002), which he directed and produced. The heist thriller featured an ensemble cast comprising Amitabh Bachchan, Sanjay Dutt, Suniel Shetty, Mahesh Manjrekar, Lucky Ali and Kumar Gaurav. Shot extensively in the United States, the movie developed a cult following for its gritty treatment, ensemble storytelling and technical presentation.

Notably, Gupta continued to explore the crime genre with projects such as Musafir (2004), while he was also associated with Shootout at Lokhandwala (2007) as a producer. He later directed Shootout at Wadala (2013), another movie centred on the Mumbai underworld. These projects further established his association with stories inspired by crime and gangland conflicts.

As per the latest buzz, His filmography also included projects beyond the gangster genre. Gupta directed the action revenge thriller Kaabil (2017), starring Hrithik Roshan, followed by the ensemble action drama Mumbai Saga (2021). Across these films, his work was marked by high-contrast visuals, stylised lighting and an emphasis on sound and action design.

In further updates, Through his production banner, White Feather Films, Gupta was involved in several projects that contributed to the evolution of the mainstream Hindi crime thriller. His approach to filmmaking and his focus on technical presentation made him a recognisable voice in the industry.

On top of that, Following reports of his passing, tributes and condolences have as per reports begun pouring in from members of the movie fraternity, collaborators and followers. Further details regarding the circumstances of his demise are awaited.

title: Ramayana advance booking crosses ₹40 crore five days before release; deadlock with Indian exhibitors ends for Ranbir Kapoor, Yash film
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

The floodgates have opened for Ramayana advance booking with less than a week to go for its big rollout. The Nitesh Tiwari movie had its world premiere in Los Angeles earlier this week, which led to a huge jump in pre-sales in the US. But back home, the movie had been crippled by a deadlock between the distributors and exhibitors, due to which many shows hadn’t opened up. On Saturday, the deadlock was finally broken, raising hopes for an increased pace of advance bookings in its final week.

Adding to this, Ranbir Kapoor stars as Lord Rama in Ramayana. How Ramayana pre-sales are faring Advance bookings for Ramayana opened on Dussehra, 15 full days before its global rollout. But for the next 10 days, only the Hindi version had extensive shows. And there, too, most of the single-screen and smaller centres had yet to open. The reason was a stalemate between the distributors and exhibitors. Dharma Productions, the movie’s distributor in India, had asked for a higher share of theatrical revenue, citing the movie's higher production costs. The distributors had shared two options: a 55% share over the first 11 days, or a three-week slab structure, with 60% going to the distributor in week 1, 50% in week 2, and 40% in week 3. The exhibitors were unwilling to give up higher revenue as they shared they were responsible for their costs. Additionally, they were wary of setting a precedent, as a settlement could prompt other big films to seek higher revenue.

Meanwhile, This led to a stalemate, with negotiations continuing for over a week. Sacnilk reported that on Friday, the deadlock was resolved, even though neither party shared the exact terms agreed upon. By Saturday, the number of screens for the movie had increased to almost 2500. By October 31 afternoon, five days before its rollout, the movie had grossed ₹ 16.5 crore rupees in advance bookings in India, selling over 3 lakh tickets. The Kannada version, which had been limited to a handful of shows, now accounted for 13% of the total gross across 150 screens. The Telugu and Tamil shows are also opening up steadily now and should be fully open by Monday.
Notably, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Ramayana: Rise of a Legend (@ramayanamovie)

As per the latest buzz, What has helped Ramayana’s case is the pre-sales buzz overseas. In North America, the movie will have paid previews on November 4, the eve of its rollout. The 24 hours after its world premiere saw the movie register a 27% jump in collections. By Friday, the movie had collected $2.5 million in overseas advance bookings, including over $1 million for the US paid previews alone. This takes the movie’s worldwide advance-booking gross to ₹ 40 crore rupees five days before its rollout.

In further updates, Produced by Namit Malhotra’s Prime Focus Studios in collaboration with DNEG and Yash’s Monster Mind Creations, Ramayana is planned as a two-part movie. The movie stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, Ravie Dubey as Lakshman, and Sunny Deol as Lord Hanuman. The first part is scheduled for worldwide rollout on November 5, 2026, while the second part is set for Diwali 2027. The films will rollout in Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam across India.

On top of that, Sony Pictures will handle global distribution, excluding India, while Dharma Productions will distribute the movie in the Hindi-speaking market. The movie is also planned for a worldwide IMAX rollout.

title: ‘A blanket order would go too far’: Madras high court refuses to restrict protests against court rulings
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Madras high court has refused to restrict public protests against court rulings and emphasised that citizens have an undeniable right to disagree with a judgment, underscoring citizens' right to “question and peacefully protest” against judicial decisions.

Adding to this, However, the court directed the state and police authorities in Tamil Nadu to “deny” permission to any gathering aimed at “personally targeting a sitting judge.” (HT File) However, the court directed the state and police authorities in Tamil Nadu to “deny” permission to any gathering aimed at “personally targeting a sitting judge.”

Meanwhile, In an order passed on Friday, October 30, a bench of Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G Arul Murugan shared authorities must assess applications seeking permission for meetings, marches or protests relating to judicial matters on a “case-by-case basis,” using their powers under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) and local police laws.

Notably, “However, the state remains under a strict obligation to ensure that its public spaces and digital networks are not used to threaten the safety and integrity of our judicial institutions,” it added.

As per the latest buzz, The court also directed the Cyber Crime Division of the Tamil Nadu police to actively monitor digital platforms to ensure that online content does not cross the line into criminal intimidation directed at sitting judges.

In further updates, It directed the police to complete their investigations into two criminal cases registered in connection with protests against a Madurai Bench judgment in a fair, thorough and expeditious manner.

On top of that, The court was hearing a public interest litigation filed by one R Karthikeyan, who sought action against organised campaigns, public meetings, processions, demonstrations and social media publications allegedly targeting judges and undermining the authority of the judiciary.

The petitioner told the court that, in a judgment passed in June last year, another bench of the Madurai bench of the Madras high court had struck down a government order concerning the grant of backwards-class benefits. At the time, the court had held that a person could not claim such benefits purely on the basis of religious conversion. The judgment had also noted that such a practice was “inconsistent with constitutional principles and Islamic theology.”

title: Sanjay Gupta remade Reservoir Dogs as Kaante; Quentin Tarantino said he loved the ‘rip-off’, called it fabulous
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Right from the start of his career, filmmaker Sanjay Gupta made a name for himself by remaking, or sometimes blatantly ripping off, Hollywood films. But his remakes often captured a new aesthetic, untapped in Indian cinema, helping them stand on their own. His most famous work is undoubtedly Kaante , the 2002 rollout that ushered in an era of stylised gangster flicks set in the US. Kaante was a remake of Quentin Tarantino’s seminal hit Reservoir Dogs, and the director went on record to say he ‘loved the rip-off’.

Adding to this, Amitabh Bachchan and Sanjay Dutt in a still from Kaante. Tarantino on Kaante Both Kaante and Reservoir Dogs were stories of six criminals coming together for a bank heist, only to be betrayed by one of their own. Reservoir Dogs, rolled out in 1992, put Tarantino on the map as a director to watch out for. Kaante, rolled out 10 years later, did the same for Sanjay Gupta. In 2007, Tarantino spoke at the Indian Movie Festival of Los Angeles, where Indian filmmaker Srinivas asked him about his opinion of Kaante. Tarantino responded, “I think it was fabulous. Of the many rip-offs, I loved Hong Kong's Too Many Ways to Be No 1 and this one, Kaante. The best part is, you have Indian guys coming to the US and looting a US bank. How cool is that! I was truly honoured. And these guys are played by legends of Bollywood.”

Meanwhile, Kaante starred Amitabh Bachchan, Sanjay Dutt, Suniel Shetty, Lucky Ali, Mahesh Manjrekar, and Kumar Gaurav in the lead roles. The movie was a moderate box-office success, earning ₹ 43 crore rupees worldwide. It was also noted for its differences with Reservoir Dogs, as it dealt with the characters’ backstories, something the Hollywood original did not. Tarantino himself noted, “Here I am, watching a movie that I've directed, and then it goes into each character's background. And I'm like, 'Whoa! For I always write backgrounds and stuff, and it always gets chopped off during the edit. And so I was amazed seeing this. I felt this isn't Reservoir Dogs, and then it goes into the warehouse scene, and I am like, 'Wow, it's back to Reservoir Dogs'. Isn't it amazing!” The filmmaker reserved some special praise for Big B, saying he particularly liked the “big beard guy, the famous guy in Bollywood’.

However, there is no official confirmation yet.

title: Ramayana international reviews hail dazzling visuals, but say exhausting narrative makes Ranbir Kapoor, Yash film an 'overproduced B movie'
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Days after its grand world premiere in Los Angeles, the first international reviews for Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana are out. The review embargo for the epic lifted on Friday night, and a handful of international publications shared their assessment of the Ranbir Kapoor and Yash-starrer. So far, the select reviews have been critical of the movie’s length and stuffed narrative, but lauded the visual effects and scale.

Adding to this, Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama. Ramayana international reviews praise visuals and scale As of Saturday morning (October 31), five major international reviews of Ramayana have been published, with two of them praising the movie wholeheartedly. However, overall, there has been praise for the movie’s visuals. Avi Offer of NYC Movie Guru called the movie ‘a visually dazzling action adventure with great set and costume design’. Similarly, Screen Rant’s Brandon Zachary rated the movie 7/10 and wrote: “On a purely visual and technical level, Ramayana: Rise of a Legend is an impressive cinematic achievement.” IndieWire gave the movie a ‘B’ and called it an ‘epic’. Reviewer Christian Zilko wrote, “( Nitesh) Tiwari appears primarily focused on dramatising the classic epic with the highest level of production value that’s currently available. He undeniably achieves that goal, even if it means that the final product lacks some voice that would have made it more memorable on its own terms.”
Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Ramayana: Rise of a Legend (@ramayanamovie)

Notably, The English version of the Ramayana is almost half an hour shorter than the Indian version. Yet the 2-and-a-half-hour runtime has not pleased early reviewers. NYC Movie Guru called the movie “bloated, clunky, exhausting, emotionally hollow and poorly acted.” Avi Offer added, “In a double feature with Sita Sings the Blues, it would be the inferior, overproduced B-movie.” Next Best Picture’s Giovanni Lago gave the movie a middling 5/10, saying the movie may have been better as a TV adaptation in the mould of Game of Thrones. “Overall, audiences can still be swept up by Ramayana, even if it feels so stuffed at times that it might’ve needed a "Game of Thrones"-level television adaptation to flesh out its narrative fully,” he wrote.

As per the latest buzz, Perhaps the harshest review of the lot was by Siddharth Adlakha of IGN, who rated the movie just 4 out of 10, writing, “A majestic epic falls victim to clunky action, eye-sore CGI, and awkward AI lip-syncing in what is, unfortunately, just a Part 1.”

In further updates, The reviews for Ramayana have only come out from the international premiere in Los Angeles so far. Indian critics have yet to watch the movie. Produced by Namit Malhotra’s Prime Focus Studios in collaboration with DNEG and Yash’s Monster Mind Creations, Ramayana is planned as a two-part movie. The movie stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, Ravie Dubey as Lakshman, and Sunny Deol as Lord Hanuman. The first part is scheduled for worldwide rollout on November 5, while the second part is set for Diwali 2027. The films will rollout in Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam across India. There are paid previews scheduled in the US on November 4, but there is no information if India will also see paid previews on the eve of rollout.

On top of that, Sony Pictures will handle global distribution, excluding India, while Dharma Productions will distribute the movie in the Hindi-speaking market. The movie is also planned for a worldwide IMAX rollout.

title: Sacred Games, Farzi motion designers call out criticism of Ramayana’s VFX, say Indians should support it ‘regardless of its flaws’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Writer-director and VFX supervisors Yashoda Parthasarthy and Vijesh Rajan, who have worked on projects such as Sacred Games , Farzi and Gangs of Wasseypur , of late opened up about the criticism surrounding the VFX of Ranbir Kapoor -starrer Ramayana.

Adding to this, Ramayana will rollout worldwide on November 5. In an exclusive conversation with Hindustan Times, the VFX supervisors called out the online criticism. They pointed out the effort that goes into making visual effects look photorealistic and echoed the movie's star and co-producer Yash's words, emphasising that films like Ramayana must be supported as they could open doors for other Indian filmmakers to reach a global audience.

Meanwhile, Speaking about supporting Ramayana, Vijesh Rajan shared, "When I was doing my MA in Movie in Australia, my thesis idea was whether an epic like Ramayana or Mahabharata could be made on the scale of The Lord of the Rings or Chronicles of Narnia. I've always dreamt of a movie like this being made. As an Indian audience, we should support such endeavors. Other than Toxic, I don't think a movie has gotten this wide rollout. It's mounted on a massive budget and is being rolled out globally on an unprecedented scale with collaborations from Hans Zimmer, AR Rahman, and top technicians. "

Notably, Vijesh emphasised that while criticism is necessary, trolling and nasty comments can leave a bad taste for filmmakers. He shared, "It is a project we should back regardless of flaws; we should discuss the flaws, but there is a way in which people speak, and that can be off-putting to a lot of filmmakers. There is a lot of trolling, and there is some sort of campaign against the movie, and I feel like, why? We should support any endeavour that is mounted on this scale. It will only open doors for other Indian filmmakers to reach the international audience, and that is a huge step."

As per the latest buzz, Yashoda, who has worked on projects such as Raman Raghav 2.0 and Ghoul, also spoke about the effort involved in creating visual effects that look realistic. She shared, "Having worked in visual effects and motion design, I remember when I was studying and 3D animation was such a difficult process in itself, and in the past decade, it has evolved a lot. But having shared that, there is a lot of work that goes into making anything photoreal and people compare our films to Marvel or Avengers movies, which have 10x the budget that we have."

In further updates, She added, “There's a lack of research, empathy, and understanding of how visual effects work. We don't support art and design, and when statements are thrown, it is a little heartbreaking because those 10,000 people have worked on it. So, definitely need to support films like Ramayana. Also, not everybody can animate, if they did, then everybody would be an expert. Let's be a little more empathetic.”

On top of that, Yashoda and Vijesh's latest short movie Aakhri Ride stars Chandan Roy and Aamir Dalvi, and features Faisal Malik in an interesting role. It is presented by Anurag Kashyap and Vasan Bala. It is produced by Ranjan Singh, Vishesh Agrawal, Rajan EPK and Anurag. It will rollout on the YouTube channel Oh Short Flips, which is curated by Anurag, on Halloween, October 31,

title: Shah Rukh Khan's King sells overseas rights for ₹175 crore, highest in Indian cinema history; film needs to out-earn Pathaan, Jawan to break even
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Even as South behemoths have conquered the Indian market with their pan-India offerings, Shah Rukh Khan remains the ‘king’ overseas. That much is evident from reports on his new movie, King , and its overseas rights deal. A new report claims that the movie’s overseas theatrical rights have been acquired for ₹ 175 crore rupees, setting a new record for Indian cinema.

Adding to this, Shah Rukh Khan's King will rollout on Christmas this year. King’s reported record overseas rights deal Pinkvilla reported that Phars Films has acquired the rights to sell the movie overseas for ₹ 175 crore rupees (over $18 million). Till now, the overseas rights of Shah Rukh’s films have been with Yash Raj Films. The company famously distributed both Pathaan (made under its own banner) and Jawan starring Shah Rukh in 2023, to great success. However, Phars also has experience in overseas distribution. It partnered with YRF on many of its films and handled Prabhas’ Saaho on its own. The Pinkvilla report states that Phars has paid a minimum guarantee (MG) amount of ₹ 175 crore rupees for King’s distribution rights. No Indian movie has reached the ₹ 100 crore rupees mark so far, which makes this achievement staggering.
Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Shah Rukh Khan (@iamsrk)

Notably, The MG amount paid for a movie reflects the distributor’s faith in its theatrical performance. Overseas, distributors usually receive only 50% of the ticket-window gross, which means that King would have to earn $37-40 million just to break even. That corresponds to around ₹ 350-375 crore rupees gross internationally. Incidentally, Shah Rukh’s two most successful films - Pathaan and Jawan - both collected around ₹ 400 crore rupees overseas. King would have to earn at least as much, if not more, to be profitable. Given this high MG, King’s overseas collections would have to be at least as high as those of Dhurandhar 2 ( ₹ 460 crore rupees) or RRR ( ₹ 430 crore rupees) to be a success there. And these are some of the biggest overseas successes in Indian cinema history.
As per the latest buzz, King stars Shah Rukh Khan in the lead role and is directed by Siddharth Anand. The movie marks Shah Rukh's second collaboration with Siddharth after the 2023 rollout, Pathaan.

In further updates, The movie also features Suhana Khan, Deepika Padukone, Abhishek Bachchan, Rani Mukerji, Jaideep Ahalawat, Raghav Juyal, Saurabh Shukla, among others. The project marks Shah Rukh's first movie with his daughter Suhana, who made her acting debut with The Archies in 2023. The movie is scheduled to arrive in theatres on December 24.

title: After Krishnavataram, Hardik Gajjar announces Tana Riri and Ajay Abhimanyu ki Mahabharat; films set for 2027 and 2028 releases
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Gajjar reunites with Krishnavataram star Sanskruti Jayana for Tana Riri , which draws from the story of the twin sisters Tana and Riri. Rooted in 16th-century Gujarat, the movie will explore the lives of the sisters from Vadnagar, who are remembered for their musical abilities and their association with the region's cultural history.

Adding to this, The first poster of the movie offers a glimpse of the period setting, featuring the twin sisters walking through the gates of a kingdom. The project aims to bring their story and its connection with Indian classical music to the big screen.
Meanwhile, Alongside Tana Riri , Gajjar is also developing Ajay Abhimanyu ki Mahabharat , a cinematic retelling centred on Abhimanyu, one of the prominent warriors from the Hindu epic.

Notably, Known for his courage and sacrifice during the Kurukshetra war, Abhimanyu's story remains one of the significant episodes in the Mahabharata. The soon-to-release movie will revisit his journey and the events associated with his role in the epic.

As per the latest buzz, Both projects are directed by Hardik Gajjar and produced by Athashrikatha Motion Pictures LLP. While Tana Riri is scheduled to arrive in cinemas in October 2027, Ajay Abhimanyu ki Mahabharat is slated for a June 2028 rollout.

In further updates, With these announcements, Gajjar has two projects in the pipeline that draw from different aspects of India's storytelling traditions, one rooted in Gujarat's cultural history and the other in the Mahabharata.

title: From Zoya Hussain in Hunkkaar 2 to Chandan Roy Sanyal in Aashram 4: 5 OTT characters we want to see return
body: Here's the latest on what's streaming and coming up:
